name: Vue
summary: A component framework that combines proxy/ref-based runtime reactivity with compiler-informed component rendering and a renderer that patches host output from reactive component effects.

features.name: Proxy and ref reactivity
features.description: Vue creates reactive objects through proxy traps and tracks ref access through getter/setter behavior, associating reactive reads with effects and triggering subscribers on writes.
benefits: Makes dependency tracking implicit for component state
Supports object and scalar reactive primitives
costs: Proxy identity and destructuring semantics can surprise users

features.name: Component render effect
features.description: Vue component instances use reactive effects around rendering, so tracked state changes schedule component updates that flow through the runtime renderer.
benefits: Connects state dependencies to view updates
Localizes update scheduling to component render effects
costs: Effect scheduling and invalidation affect update timing
Deep reactive conversion may add work for large state graphs

features.name: Compiler-informed host patching
features.description: Vue's runtime renderer creates component and element renderers and patches host output; compiler-generated vnode shape information can inform which parts require dynamic updates.
benefits: Uses compilation knowledge to reduce some runtime work
costs: Compiler and runtime contracts must remain compatible
Virtual-node identity and patch rules add framework semantics

mathematical_views.question: Which effects are reachable from a reactive property read and therefore eligible for re-execution after mutation?
assumptions: Reactive targets and keys are graph nodes
Reads create dependency edges to active effects
Scheduler batching is abstracted as an execution policy

mathematical_views.question: How does invalidated component state transition from a render effect to host-node patches?
assumptions: A component render produces a vnode relation
The renderer compares old and new vnode structures
DOM and platform operations are abstracted behind host operations

mathematical_views.question: Which compiler annotations can constrain runtime patch work without changing the component state graph?
assumptions: Compiler output and runtime renderer share a vnode contract
Optimization hints describe dynamic regions rather than proving performance
Template compilation is modeled as a transformation boundary

costs: Runtime graph maintenance and proxy edge cases remain visible
Effect invalidation and batching complicate timing

benefits: Compiler knowledge can reduce runtime work
costs: Build-time and runtime versions must preserve shared contracts
